records.name: Bridesburg Community Action Alliance
records.summary: If you care about what gets built near you, Bridesburg Community Action Alliance is a City registered community organization in the River Wards part of the city that hears about zoning and development proposals.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over.

locations.label: Meeting place (City list)
locations.address: Bridesburg Recreation Center, 4625 Richmond Street, Philadelphia, PA 19137

locations.label: Contact address (City list)
locations.address: C/O Yvonne Stephens, 4507 E Thompson Street, Philadelphia, PA 19137

first_step.how: Call the contact on the City list, Yvonne Stephens at 215-915-0078, and ask when and where the next meeting is held.
first_step.basis: No meeting schedule, agenda or join steps were published that we could read, and the only public web link is a Facebook group page, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: We could not confirm what a visit is like, because no schedule or agenda was published that we could read. The City lists the group as one that reviews zoning and development plans with neighbors.

records.notes: The only web link is a Facebook group page. Facebook is leads only and was not read. A web search for the group found no page about it, so no meeting schedule or join steps are recorded. The meeting place comes from the City list; the Thompson Street address is a contact (mailing) address. Kept as publish with low confidence because the group is City registered and a contact is named. Re-check before relying on it.

records.name: Community Schools @John H. Webster
records.summary: John H. Webster Elementary is a kindergarten to 5th grade school on Frankford Avenue and part of the City's Community Schools program. Volunteers help hand out groceries to families each week and support school events now and then.
records.what_you_do: Help hand out groceries to students and families, or lend a hand with school events.

schedule.text: Grocery distribution to students and families each week, plus school events now and then

first_step.how: Complete the clearances listed on the City's volunteer portal, then sign up there for an open grocery or events shift.
first_step.basis: A first shift needs several school and state clearances, so the way in is paperwork first. The school's own site describes no volunteer route.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers must finish the clearances before their first shift, so the first step is paperwork rather than a visit. The listing does not say how long a shift lasts.
first_visit_tips: Start the clearances early, since they must be finished before any shift.
Ask the Community Schools office which opening is current before you sign up.

records.notes: The City volunteer listing returned HTTP 403 to this run and was not retried. The shift, clearance and weekly details are carried from the tier 1 read made on 2026-10-08 and were not re-checked. The clearances are recorded as two yes flags, not copied as a list. The school's own site gives the main phone as 215-400-7170 (not added to contacts). Its Parent Volunteers page returned 404. The school site does not describe the Community Schools program or name a coordinator.

records.name: Community Schools @Kensington Health Sciences Academy
records.summary: Kensington Health Sciences Academy is a public high school for grades 9 to 12 on Emerald Street and part of the City's Community Schools program. It takes volunteers through the City's portal, but none were listed when we last checked.
records.what_you_do: Help with school-based programs for students and families when a volunteer need is posted.

first_step.how: No volunteer need was listed when the City portal was last read, so call the school at 215-400-3600 and ask whether the team needs volunteers right now.
first_step.basis: No open volunteer role was listed when last checked, and the school's own site gives no volunteer or visitor steps, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: We could not confirm what a visit is like, because the school's site does not describe volunteer work and no opening was listed. Ask the school before you plan a first visit.
first_visit_tips: Call before you go, since no opening is listed right now.
The school's site does not publish visitor rules, so ask about them when you call.

records.notes: The City volunteer listing returned HTTP 403 to this run and was not retried. records.name: East Kensington Neighbors Association
records.summary: East Kensington neighbors who meet once a month to share concerns and run committees for cleanups, greening, youth programs, historic preservation, and zoning. A member can join a committee or simply come to the monthly meeting.
records.what_you_do: Join a committee (cleanups and community affairs, greening, youth and education, historic preservation, zoning, or green space), or come to the monthly meeting to raise concerns and hear updates.

schedule.text: General membership meeting on the 3rd Monday of the month at 7 pm. Zoning meeting on the 2nd Wednesday at 7 pm. No meetings in August.

cost.text: Meetings are open to all with no membership fee.

access.notes: The monthly meeting is also livestreamed on Zoom. Joining online needs a short registration and an address or business in the East Kensington boundaries.

first_step.how: Come to the monthly general meeting on the 3rd Monday at 7 pm, and say you are new, since the agenda opens by welcoming new residents. To ask first, email info@ekna.org.
first_step.basis: The meeting agenda starts by welcoming new residents, the meeting is open to all with no fee, and the group's pages say how to attend.
first_step.what_to_expect: The general meeting starts at 7 pm and the community calendar lists it ending around 8:30 pm. The agenda opens with a welcome to new residents, then officer reports, cleanup and greening news, a quarterly crime report from the local police precinct, and an open forum for neighbors. There is no membership fee to attend.
first_visit_tips: Arrive a few minutes before 7 pm to find a seat.
Say you are new when you arrive, since the agenda welcomes new residents.
To join by Zoom, register ahead and have proof of an East Kensington address or business.
There is no meeting in August, so plan around that.

records.notes: The group's own pages are current: monthly meeting page, calendar, Get Involved and committee names. Contact differences: the group's site gives its office as 2439 Amber Street, info@ekna.org and 215-334-EKNA. The City list gave 2440 Frankford Ave, president@ekna.org and 267-601-1366. Both are kept, the City address is labelled as such. The meeting place is named as Philadelphia Brewing Company with no street address on the pages read. The calendar lists the meeting at 7 to 8:30 pm for Oct 19, 2026, from the NKCDC calendar, used for the end time and the sign of life. The newsletter page shows an editor note that its sign-up storage is not set up, so signup may not work; no form was submitted. The committees URL returned 404; committee names come from Get Involved. Greening and green space work is tagged vacant_lot_greening, the closest tag available. No newsletter issues are listed.

records.name: Fishtown Kensington Area Business Improvement District
records.notes: Judgment call for the owner. Verdict is hide (out_of_scope, the rule for businesses with no community program) because the district's own home page describes mainly promoting member businesses. It names Clean and Green, Safe and Secure, and Beautification sections but gives no detail, and shows no public meeting, volunteer route or resident program. It is on the City RCO list as a registered community organization, so overrule to publish if its zoning role counts as civic. The site's office phone is (267) 764-3724, which differs from the City list number. Only the home page was read; it gave no program detail to follow.

records.name: Harrowgate Civic Association
records.summary: Harrowgate Civic Association is a Registered Community Organization (RCO) in the River Wards part of the city. The City asks developers to talk with RCOs about nearby zoning and building plans, so this is a way for neighbors to have a say.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together each month to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

schedule.text: Monthly general neighbors' meeting, 6:30 to 8:30 pm

first_step.how: Go to the monthly neighbors' meeting, which runs 6:30 to 8:30 pm. The calendar does not give the room, so email harrowgatecivicassociation@gmail.com first to confirm the next date and place.
first_step.basis: A community calendar lists a monthly neighbors' meeting, and the group gives an email and phone number. No page says how first-timers are welcomed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The monthly meeting runs about two hours in the evening, from 6:30 to 8:30 pm on the calendar. The calendar does not describe the agenda, whether the meeting is in person or online, or who usually attends, so ask the group before your first visit.
first_visit_tips: Email the group before the meeting to confirm the date and room.
Bring a question about a nearby building or zoning plan, since that is the group's main work.

records.notes: No group website of its own: the only web link is a Facebook group page. Facebook is leads only and was not read. The monthly meeting comes from a community calendar on nkcdc.org (the Oct 1, 2026 meeting, 6:30 to 8:30 pm, place not stated). The calendar's header covers late September through October 2026. A web search found nothing about the group. The meeting place and contact address are from the City list, and no source gives the room.

records.name: New Kensington CDC
records.summary: New Kensington CDC is a community-based nonprofit that helps neighbors with housing counseling and home repairs, small business help, and health and gardening programs. It also works with the City on local priorities and is a registered community organization for zoning talks.
records.what_you_do: Get help with housing or a small business, join the Saturday gardening club, or sign up as a Community Connector to build skills and connect with a wider network.

schedule.text: Weekend Gardening Club on Saturdays, 10 am to noon, for adults. Cure Violence Kensington walk-in hours on Fridays, 2 to 4 pm.

cost.text: The group says many services are free. The cost of the gardening club and walk-in hours is not stated.

first_step.how: Come to the Saturday Weekend Gardening Club at 10 am. The group's pages do not give the place or cost, so call 215-427-0350 first to confirm.
first_step.basis: Friday hours are a walk-in space, and the group lists a phone, email and text line. The gardening club is for adults building skills, but its listing gives no sign-up step.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Saturday gardening club runs 10 am to noon for adults who want to build gardening skills and share what they know. Friday walk-in hours run 2 to 4 pm, and you can drop by without an appointment. Neither listing gives the place or cost, so ask first.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-427-0350 or email info@nkcdc.org to confirm the place for the gardening club.
Text the word NKCDC to 833-901-2072 to get event alerts.
Wear clothes you can get dirty if you plan to garden.

records.notes: The group's own site is current, with dated events for October 2026. The site gives 19134 as the zip for 2771 Ruth Street, Suite 1, while the City list gave 19125 for the same address.
